docs.title: MiCoKnowGraph
docs.text: A draft data model for a microbiome knowledge graph (KG), written as a starting point for BioHackathon Europe 2026, Project 16. Source: https://github.com/FatemehFN/micokg-blueprint.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text: You are… Read New to the project Onboarding: set up and run everything New to RDF, ontologies or SPARQL Knowledge-graph primer Adding classes, slots or data Modelling guide A domain expert with questions the KG should answer Use cases Working on mappings or VERDANT VERDANT integration Wondering why something is modelled the way it is The design notes, starting with associations as nodes

docs.title: The design in one picture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  subgraph Entities["Entities (ontology IRIs)"]
    T[Taxon<br/>NCBITaxon]
    D[Disease<br/>MONDO]
    M[Metabolite<br/>ChEBI]
    G[Gene / AMR determinant<br/>GO, ARO, SO]
    F[Food<br/>FoodOn]
  end
  S[Sample<br/>MIxS + ENVO/UBERON] -->|hasFeatureOfInterest ◀| O[Observation<br/>SOSA]
  O -->|is about| T
  O -->|is about| G
  A((Association<br/>direction, site,<br/>evidence, study)) -->|rdf:subject| T
  A -->|rdf:object| D
  A -->|derived from| O
  X[[SSSOM mappings]] -.->|exactMatch| D
  • Observations are raw per-sample measurements.
  • Associations are claims made from them (or taken from the literature) and carry their context and evidence.
  • Mappings connect identifiers from different ontologies, so a DOID-coded record from one resource still answers a MONDO-coded question.

docs.title: Competency questions from the coordination sheet
docs.text:
The team's use cases and competency questions (CQs) live in the project's coordination sheet. This page checks the nine CQs written there (as of 8 November 2026) against the schema in this repository: what each one needs, what the schema already holds, and what would have to be added. It ends with the additions in priority order and a suggestion for which CQs to translate into SPARQL first.

The CQs are quoted in short form; the full text, entities and relationships are in the sheet ("Task 1 - Competency Questions").

docs.title: Use cases: sheet versus this repository
docs.text: Sheet Owner Repository Fit Use case 1, Photosynthetic biodiversity and activity in clouds Bérénice UC1 Aeromicrobiome Same domain (air samples, taxa, gene functions). The sheet's version is about one site (Puy de Dôme), photosynthetic organisms, and many physical measurements. Use case 2, Plasmids in the microbiome of diseases, especially cancer Niko UC2 AMR transmission and UC3 Host–microbiome in cancer Covers both: taxa associated with tumours (UC3) and AMR genes on mobile elements (UC2). Plasmids as objects in their own right are new. Use case 3, Sociability and gut bacteria in a macaque population Caprice none New. Needs host-level behaviour and health attributes; see the end of this page. Use case 4 not started Use case 5, SynCom traits in crop biocontrol Pedro none New. Needs field-trial design, treatments and synthetic communities; see the end of this page. none UC4 Nutrition Not in the sheet. Kept as it exercises diet, taxon, metabolite and disease chains, which CQ 9 also needs.

docs.title: How to read the verdicts
docs.text:
• Answerable now: the schema holds the data and the query can be written against the toy data.
  • Small addition: a slot, enum or class is missing; the addition is listed and is a few lines of LinkML.
  • Not a schema question: the relationship in the sheet is a comparison or statistic that a query computes (comparedTo, differsFrom, hasSimilarity), or a mechanistic claim that would only ever be a literature statement with free text behind it. These are noted and not modelled.

docs.title: CQ 1. Taxa, diversity indices and abundances of photosynthetic versus non-photosynthetic organisms in cloud samples at Puy de Dôme
docs.text:
Needs Status Samples at a named site, with date, coordinates, altitude, sampling method and weather Sample has geo_location, geo_loc_name, latitude, longitude, collection_date, env_* (ENVO). Altitude and weather are not slots; they can be sample-level observations (addition 1) or MIxS air-package slots. Relative or absolute abundance of a taxon in a sample (hasAbundance) Answerable now: Observation with observed_property relative_abundance, is_about the taxon, simple_result, unit (cells/m³, gene copies). Diversity indices per sample (hasDiversityMetric) Small addition 1: a Shannon index is about the sample, not a taxon, but is_about is required. Grouping taxa as photosynthetic or not (belongsToGroup) Small addition 4: a taxon-level trait, e.g. taxon capable of photosynthesis (GO:0015979). Cyanobacteria can also be found by taxonomy alone. comparedTo Not a schema question: the query groups by trait and compares.

Verdict: small additions 1 and 4. The taxon-and-abundance half is answerable now.

docs.title: CQ 2. Physiological state of photosynthetic organisms and the effect of stressors on photosynthetic efficiency
docs.text:
Needs Status Measurements per sample or per organism: PSII yield, chlorophyll fluorescence, pigments, carbon fixation rate, gene expression (psbA, rbcL) Addition 1 for sample-level values; gene expression is an Observation is_about a FunctionalGene with a new observed property (expression) and unit. Stressor levels (UV index, temperature, pH, nutrients) Addition 1: sample-level observations, or MIxS slots. Physiological state as a category (active, dormant, stressed, damaged) Small addition 2: simple_result is numeric only; categorical results need an ontology-term result. influencedBy: stressor changes efficiency Not a schema question in this round; it is a finding, not a measurement. Could later be an association between an exposure and a process.

Verdict: small additions 1 and 2 for the measurements; the mechanistic half is not modelled.

docs.title: CQ 3. Enriched carbon-fixation pathways and genes, compared with non-photosynthetic organisms
docs.text:
Needs Status Genes (cbbL, ccmK, prk, ppc) with function and host taxon (exhibitsGene) Answerable now: FunctionalGene with gene_symbol, has_function (GO), gene_family (KO, EC), in_taxon. Pathways (hasMetabolicPathway) GO biological processes cover them (e.g. GO:0015977 carbon fixation, GO:0019253 reductive pentose-phosphate cycle). A KEGG pathway identifier can go in gene_family today; a Pathway class is optional. Gene presence or abundance per sample Answerable now (gene_presence; add an abundance or expression property). Enzyme activity, carbon flux, measured under conditions (measuredUnder) Addition 1: sample-level observations; conditions are other observations on the same sample, joined by sample. comparesTo Not a schema question.

Verdict: answerable now for genes and pathways; addition 1 for the rates.

docs.title: CQ 4. Metabolic by-products and their effect on cloud chemistry
docs.text:
Needs Status Organism produces by-product (producesByproduct) Answerable now: TaxonMetaboliteAssociation with RO:0002234 has output and a ChEBI object (oxalic acid, hydrogen peroxide, isoprene). Cloud chemistry parameters (pH, ROS, ions) per sample Addition 1. By-product changes a parameter (influencesChemistry, hasMechanism) Not a schema question in this round: chemistry and mechanism belong to the literature, not the KG's measurements.

Verdict: answerable now for production; addition 1 for chemistry; mechanisms not modelled.

docs.title: CQ 5. Biogeographical differences between Puy de Dôme and other sites
docs.text:
Needs Status Sites and their community composition (hasComposition) Answerable now: aggregate observations by geo_location. Atmospheric conditions per site Addition 1. Functional traits of taxa (hasTrait, adaptsTo) Addition 4 (taxon trait association). Ecological interactions (interactsWith) Answerable now: TaxonHostAssociation with RO:0002437 biotically interacts with; competition and mutualism are RO sub-relations and could be allowed in the predicate pattern. differsFrom, hasSimilarity Not a schema question: beta diversity is computed.

Verdict: small additions 1 and 4.

docs.title: CQ 6. Diurnal, cloud-lifecycle and seasonal variation of photosynthetic activity
docs.text:
Needs Status Time of day of sampling Small addition 3: collection_date is a date; a datetime, or a separate time slot, is needed for day/night. Cloud lifecycle stage and season as sample attributes Addition 3: a categorical sampling-context slot (or a categorical observation, addition 2). Activity metrics and gene expression over time Addition 1 plus result_time, which exists. variesWith, drivenBy, correlatesWith, hasAmplitude Not a schema question: computed over the time series.

Verdict: small additions 1, 2 and 3.

docs.title: CQ 7. Taxa, plasmid replicons, diversity and abundance in tumour versus adjacent normal tissue and healthy controls
docs.text:
Needs Status Specimen from a body site, with pathology status (sampledFrom) host_body_site (UBERON) exists. Tumour versus adjacent normal versus healthy is a small addition 3: a sample condition slot (NCIT or MONDO term). Specimen type (FFPE, fresh-frozen, stool, cell-free DNA) is a second slot in the same addition. Patient's cancer type Answerable now: Host.has_disease (MONDO). Taxon abundance per sample Answerable now. Plasmids with replicon type, mobility class, copy number, host taxon (harboursPlasmid, hasMobilityClass, hasCopyNumber) Small addition 5: a Plasmid (mobile genetic element) class. Today only genes know they sit on a plasmid (genomic_context SO:0000155). Diversity indices Addition 1. Fold change, p-values, LDA scores, tumour versus normal (comparedTo) Answerable now as claims: TaxonDiseaseAssociation with direction, effect_size, p_value, anatomical_context, has_evidence, source_study. The existing query uc3-cq01 (taxa associated with colorectal cancer, with direction and evidence) is a working subset of this CQ.

Verdict: small additions 1, 3 and 5. The differential-abundance half is answerable now.

docs.title: CQ 8. Longitudinal resistome and plasmid evolution across clinical milestones
docs.text:
Needs Status AMR genes with ARO class, drug class, mechanism, on plasmids Answerable now: AMRDeterminant with aro_class, confers_resistance_to, resistance_mechanism, genomic_context. Repeated samples from one patient over time Answerable now: Sample.has_host plus collection_date. Clinical milestones and treatments with dates (variesAcrossTimepoint, drivenBySelectivePressure, hasBaseline) Small addition 6: host-level events (antibiotic given, chemotherapy, surgery, relapse) with a type and a date, so observations can be placed before or after them. Genes co-located on one plasmid (coSelectedWith) Addition 5: a plasmid record that lists the genes it carries. exhibitsEvolutionaryShift (IS26 amplification, co-integrates, SNPs) Not a schema question in this round: genome-structure findings per strain are better kept in the source data and cited. precedesClinicalEvent Derivable from dates once addition 6 exists; the causal reading stays with the literature.

Verdict: small additions 5 and 6; the AMR gene layer is answerable now.

docs.title: CQ 9. Antibiotics before immunotherapy: depletion of commensals, resistome expansion, metabolites and treatment response
docs.text:
Needs Status Antibiotic decreases a taxon (depletesTaxon) Nearly now: DietTaxonAssociation accepts a CHEBI subject and direction decreased, but its name says diet. Small addition 7: rename it to an exposure-to-taxon association that covers foods and drugs. Taxon produces metabolite, metabolite linked to outcome (reducesMetabolite, impairsImmunePriming) Taxon to metabolite answerable now. Metabolite to outcome exists for diseases (MetaboliteDiseaseAssociation); immune processes would need GO or HP objects allowed in its pattern. Resistome load and plasmid richness per sample (enrichesPlasmidome) Answerable now for genes (observations about AMRDeterminant records, aggregated); plasmids need addition 5. Therapy, exposure window and response (attenuatesEfficacyOf, stratifiesPatientBy) Addition 6: events with dates, plus a response outcome on the host or the event. Stratification is then a query.

Verdict: small additions 5, 6 and 7; the immunology chain is partly literature-only.

docs.title: Additions, in priority order
docs.text:
Each serves several CQs. None changes the three-layer design; they are slots, one enum and two classes.

# Addition Serves Sketch 1 Sample-level observations. Make Observation.is_about optional, so a measurement can be about the sample as a whole; publish a controlled list of observed properties (relative abundance, gene presence, gene expression, Shannon index, Simpson index, richness, pH, temperature, UV index, cell count, ...) with the ontology term where one exists (PATO, STATO, UO for units). CQ 1–7 is_about: required: false; observed_property bound to a micokg:property/... list documented in the modelling guide. 2 Categorical results. Add result_term (sosa:hasResult, range uriorcurie) beside simple_result, for states such as dormant or stressed. CQ 2, 6 one slot 3 Sample condition and context. Add sample_condition (NCIT/MONDO/PATO term: malignant tumour, adjacent normal, healthy control), specimen_type (OBI/NCIT: FFPE, fresh-frozen, stool, cfDNA), and either make collection_date a datetime or add collection_time; optionally a sampling_context note for cloud stage or season. CQ 6, 7 three slots on Sample 4 Taxon trait association. TaxonTraitAssociation: subject taxon, predicate RO:0002215 capable of (or RO:0000053 has characteristic), object GO process or PATO/OMP trait (photosynthesis, UV resistance, desiccation tolerance). CQ 1, 3, 5 one association class, same slots as the others 5 Plasmid class. MobileGeneticElement (or Plasmid): identifier (PLSDB accession or minted), replicon_type (text: IncF, IncI1, ColRNAI), mobility_class enum (conjugative, mobilisable, non-mobilisable), in_taxon (host), carries_gene (multivalued, to FunctionalGene/AMRDeterminant). Observations may be about it (abundance, copy number). CQ 7, 8, 9 one class, one enum, four slots 6 Host events. HostEvent: host, event_type (NCIT or CHEBI: antibiotic administration with the drug, chemotherapy, surgery, immune checkpoint blockade, relapse), start_date, end_date, optional outcome (responder, non-responder). CQ 8, 9; also UC3 macaques and UC5 field trials one class 7 Exposure association. Rename DietTaxonAssociation and DietMetaboliteAssociation to ExposureTaxonAssociation and ExposureMetaboliteAssociation, subject FOODON, CHEBI or NCIT (foods, drugs, antibiotics). CQ 9, UC4 rename plus pattern

Not planned: storing comparisons (comparedTo, differsFrom, hasSimilarity), and mechanistic statements (influencesChemistry, hasMechanism, exhibitsEvolutionaryShift, impairsImmunePriming). The first group is computed by queries; the second would need free-text claims, which the sheet's own ontology column cannot ground either.

docs.title: Ontologies named in the sheet
docs.text: The nine CQs name ENVO, PROV, NCBITAXON, GO, CHEBI, UBERON, MONDO, ARO, SO, OBI and RO. All are prefixes in the schema and used by at least one slot. Two are not: PO (Plant Ontology, named for CQ 2; it would only matter if plant hosts enter, as in Use case 5) and BERO (named for Use case 2 in the sheet; it is in the Ontologies tab but not in any CQ). The sheet's "Classes / concepts" column currently lists only PROV terms (Entity, Collection, Location, atLocation); the schema places those on Study (PROV/DCTerms) and Sample (geo_location).

docs.title: The two new use cases
docs.text:
Use case 3, macaques (Caprice). Hosts are Macaca mulatta (Host.in_taxon), samples are faeces (env_medium UBERON:0001988), taxa and diversity come from observations (addition 1). What is missing is host-level data: sociability score, grooming rate, social rank, immune status, sampling period. The cleanest route is to let an Observation have a Host as its feature of interest (today only Sample), so behaviour and health scores are observations on the animal with a date; the CQ then joins host observations to sample observations. That is addition 1 plus a one-line range change.

Use case 5, SynCom in crop biocontrol (Pedro). Soil and plant-tissue samples fit Sample (ENVO soil terms; plant tissue as env_medium with PO terms, which would bring PO in). New: a SyntheticCommunity entity (member strains, delivery formulation), a field trial with blocks and treatments (addition 6 generalised to events on plots, not hosts), pathogen pressure and yield as outcomes. This is the furthest from the current schema and should wait for the CQs to be written.

docs.title: Suggested order of work
docs.text:
1. CQ 7, differential-abundance half. Runs today on uc3-cq01; retarget the question text and toy data to tumour versus adjacent normal tissue with anatomical_context, and paste the query into the sheet's translation column.
  2. CQ 1, taxa-and-abundance half. Needs toy cloud samples (ENVO cloud terms, Puy de Dôme coordinates) and relative-abundance observations; one query, answerable today. Diversity indices follow once addition 1 is in.
  3. Additions 1 and 5, which unlock the rest of CQ 1 and CQ 7 and most of CQ 8.
  4. Then CQ 3 (genes and pathways, mostly answerable now) and CQ 8.

docs.title: Knowledge-graph primer
docs.text: This page is for people who work comfortably with dataframes, pipelines or ML, but haven't worked with RDF, ontologies or SPARQL. Each idea links to where it shows up in this repository.

docs.title: 1. Triples: a graph as a three-column table
docs.text:
A knowledge graph is a set of triples: subject – predicate – object.

subject predicate object NCBITaxon:851 rdfs:label "Fusobacterium nucleatum" micokg:sample/UC3-S01 mixs:0000014 (env_medium) UBERON:0001988 (feces) micokg:obs/UC3-O01 sosa:hasSimpleResult 0.042

If you know PyTorch Geometric: subjects and objects are nodes, and each predicate is an edge type. The graph is heterogeneous by nature. The difference from an edge_index is that every node and edge type has a globally unique name, so graphs from different groups can simply be merged.

This format is called RDF, and .ttl (Turtle) files are one way to write it. Run make rdf and open build/rdf/Container-uc3-cancer.ttl to see our toy data as triples.

docs.title: 2. IRIs and CURIEs: global names
docs.text:
Every node and predicate is named by an IRI, a web address such as http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/NCBITaxon_851. Writing that in full is tedious, so we use CURIEs (NCBITaxon:851) plus a prefix map that expands them. The prefix map is in schema/micokg.yaml.

The golden rule: if an ontology already has an identifier for the thing, use it. Two resources that both say NCBITaxon:851 are automatically about the same organism, with no joining on fuzzy names.

docs.title: 3. Ontologies: controlled vocabularies with a hierarchy
docs.text:
An ontology is a curated set of terms with definitions and relations, most importantly is_a (rdfs:subClassOf):

colorectal adenocarcinoma (MONDO:0005008)
  is_a colorectal carcinoma
    is_a colorectal cancer (MONDO:0005575)

So a question about colorectal cancer should also find records coded as colorectal adenocarcinoma. The ontologies used here, by entity:

Entity Ontology Taxa NCBITaxon Environments ENVO Anatomy UBERON Diseases MONDO / DOID / NCIT / EFO Chemicals and metabolites ChEBI Functions GO Sequence features SO Antimicrobial resistance ARO Foods FoodOn Evidence types ECO

Browse any of them in OLS. For offline tests we keep slims: the is_a ancestors of only the terms we use, in examples/ontology-slims/.

docs.title: 4. LinkML: the schema you edit
docs.text:
Hand-writing RDF is error-prone, so we describe the data model in LinkML, a YAML schema language similar in spirit to pydantic models or JSON Schema. From one schema we get:

  • validation of YAML/JSON data (make validate);
  • RDF conversion, where every slot has a slot_uri that becomes the predicate;
  • OWL, SHACL, a JSON-LD context and documentation (make gen).

A slot definition looks like this:

env_medium:
  slot_uri: mixs:0000014        # the RDF predicate (reused from the MIxS standard)
  range: uriorcurie             # the value is an identifier, so it becomes an IRI in RDF
  pattern: "^(ENVO:\\d{8}|UBERON:\\d{7})$"

Contributors mostly write YAML data that follows the schema (see examples/valid/). They rarely write RDF directly.

docs.title: 5. Observations vs associations
docs.text:
Two kinds of statement are easily confused:

  • Observation (SOSA standard): in sample S01, the relative abundance of F. nucleatum was 0.042. This is a raw measurement.
  • Association: F. nucleatum is increased in colorectal cancer (stool, study A, experimental evidence). This is a claim made from observations or from a paper.

A plain edge F.nucleatum → correlated_with → CRC has nowhere to store increased, stool, which study or how confident. And when another study finds the opposite, the two findings collapse into one edge. So each association is a node of its own (in RDF terms, a reified statement):

micokg:assoc/UC3-A03  rdf:subject    NCBITaxon:817
                      rdf:predicate  RO:0002610       # correlated with
                      rdf:object     MONDO:0005575
                      micokg:direction "increased"
                      micokg:anatomical_context UBERON:0001988
                      dct:source     micokg:study/UC3-A

In graph-ML terms, the edge now has attributes, or you can think of it as a hyperedge. For tools that want plain edges, scripts/materialise_shortcuts.rq derives them. See ADR-0001.

docs.title: 6. SPARQL: querying the graph
docs.text:
SPARQL matches patterns of triples. Variables start with ?:

SELECT ?taxon ?direction WHERE {
  ?a a micokg:TaxonDiseaseAssociation ;      # ?a is a taxon–disease association
     rdf:subject ?taxon ;                    # about some taxon
     rdf:object  ?disease ;                  # and some disease
     micokg:direction ?direction .
  ?disease rdfs:subClassOf* obo:MONDO_0005575 .   # the disease is CRC or any subtype
}
  • ; repeats the same subject.
  • rdfs:subClassOf* is a property path meaning "zero or more is_a steps".
  • skos:exactMatch|^skos:exactMatch means "a mapping in either direction".

All our questions are in queries/, with comments explaining each part. Run them with python scripts/run_cq.py.

docs.title: 7. SSSOM: mappings between ontologies
docs.text: Different resources code the same concept differently, e.g. DOID:9256 and MONDO:0005575 for colorectal cancer. SSSOM is a TSV format for such mappings. Each row records the match type (skos:exactMatch, closeMatch…), how it was made (manual curation, lexical match, or an AI model such as VERDANT) and who made or reviewed it. See mappings/ and VERDANT integration.

docs.title: 8. SHACL: shape checks on RDF
docs.text: SHACL describes what well-formed RDF looks like ("every association has exactly one rdf:subject, and it is an IRI"). We generate it from the LinkML schema and check the converted examples (make shacl).

docs.text:

docs.title: Modelling guide
docs.text: These are the conventions used in schema/ and examples/. The reasons behind them are in the design notes in docs/adr/.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
1. Competency questions drive the model. Every class or slot should serve at least one question in queries/. If no question needs it, it waits.
  2. Reuse before you invent.
  3. Use an existing ontology identifier for things: NCBITaxon, ENVO, MONDO, ChEBI and so on.
  4. Use an existing standard property for relations: MIxS, SOSA, RO, DCTERMS, PROV.
  5. Mint micokg: terms only when nothing fits, and write down why.
  6. Keep measurements separate from claims. Per-sample measurements are Observations. Generalised or literature-derived statements are Associations.
  7. Keep context with the claim. Direction, body site, environment, host, evidence and source live on the association node (ADR-0001).

docs.title: Identifiers
docs.text:
Kind of thing Identifier Example Organism, habitat, anatomy, disease, chemical, function, AMR gene family Ontology CURIE NCBITaxon:851, ENVO:00002005, ARO:3000186 Sample, observation, association, study, host, gene record Minted micokg:<type>/<local-id> micokg:sample/UC3-S01 Person ORCID ORCID:0000-0002-... Publication doi: or PMID: doi:10.1234/abcd Source resource infores CURIE infores:gutmdisorder

Type segments currently in use: study, sample, host, obs, assoc, gene, property.

docs.title: Slots with ontology values
docs.text:
Ontology-valued slots have range: uriorcurie and a pattern restricting the prefix, and they may declare bindings to a dynamic enum (the allowed ontology branch):

env_medium:
  slot_uri: mixs:0000014
  range: uriorcurie
  pattern: "^(ENVO:\\d{8}|UBERON:\\d{7})$"
  bindings:
    - range: EnvironmentalMaterialEnum
      obligation_level: RECOMMENDED

Why not an enum? LinkML writes enum values to RDF as string literals, but queries need IRIs so that they can follow rdfs:subClassOf. tests/test_rdf_shacl.py::test_ontology_slots_are_iris guards this. Static enums are fine for small internal code lists such as direction and compartment.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text:
• Classes are UpperCamelCase; slots and enum values are snake_case.
  • Association classes are named <Subject><Object>Association, or ...Interaction for organism–organism.
  • Every slot has a slot_uri. Choose, in order:
  • an established standard (MIxS, SOSA, DCTERMS, PROV, SKOS, RDFS);
  • an OBO Relation Ontology property (RO);
  • micokg:<slot_name>.

docs.title: Adding a new association type (worked recipe)
docs.text:
Example: taxon produces a quorum-sensing molecule that affects host inflammation.

  1. Write the competency question first.
  2. Check whether an existing class fits. Here TaxonMetaboliteAssociation plus MetaboliteDiseaseAssociation already chain.

  3. If a new class is needed, add it to schema/associations.yaml:

    TaxonPhenotypeAssociation:
  is_a: Association
  class_uri: micokg:TaxonPhenotypeAssociation
  description: A taxon is associated with a host phenotype.
  slot_usage:
    subject:
      pattern: "^(NCBITaxon:\\d+|GTDB:.+)$"
    predicate:
      pattern: "^RO:(0002610|0003302)$"
    object:
      pattern: "^(HP|MP|NCIT):[A-Za-z0-9_]+$"

  4. Add a list slot to Container in schema/micokg.yaml (taxon_phenotype_associations), and any new prefixes.

  5. Add toy data to examples/valid/, plus an examples/invalid/ file showing a common mistake.
  6. Add the .rq query and the cqs.yaml entry, then run make slims (for the new terms) and make test.

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
• observed_property is a micokg:property/... IRI for now (relative_abundance, gene_presence). Open question: adopt a published property vocabulary (e.g. from OBA, STATO or the MIxS measurement terms).
  • simple_result is a number. Use 0 for "tested and not detected", and simply leave out things that weren't tested.
  • used_procedure should point to an OBI assay or a bio.tools/WorkflowHub identifier.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text: # Question Current choice 1 MONDO or DO as the preferred disease ontology? MONDO first; DO/NCIT/EFO accepted, bridged by SSSOM 2 NCBITaxon vs GTDB for MAG-derived taxa Both accepted; mapping file needed 3 Plasmid is not under mobile_genetic_element in SO. How should "mobile context" be modelled? Queries list both roots 4 How to represent negative findings (no association found)? negated: true; excluded from shortcuts 5 Meaning and calibration of confidence across sources Free float 0–1; needs a definition 6 Units and normalisation for abundance unit slot; no vocabulary chosen yet (QUDT/UO?) 7 Imaging and clinical data Future modules (imaging.yaml, clinical.yaml) 8 Individual-level host data and privacy Hosts are pseudonymous toy records; real data only aggregated? 9 Reification in RDF 1.2 (triple terms) vs association nodes Association nodes (see ADR-0001)

docs.title: Onboarding
docs.text: Goal: go from a fresh clone to a green make all and your first query.

docs.title: 1. Set up the environment
docs.text:
You need Python 3.12 or 3.13. LinkML does not support 3.14 yet. Java and Docker are not needed.

git clone https://github.com/FatemehFN/micokg-blueprint.git && cd micokg-blueprint
mamba env create -f environment.yml      # conda works too
mamba activate micokg

If conda activate / mamba activate does not work in your shell

Run commands through the environment instead: mamba run -n micokg make all. Or put it on your PATH for the session: export PATH="$HOME/miniforge3/envs/micokg/bin:$PATH".

Without conda:

python3.12 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -e ".[dev]"

docs.title: 2. Build and test everything
docs.text:
make all

Everything in make all works offline. Only make slims and make terms need internet access.

This runs, in order:

Target What it does lint linkml-lint style and consistency checks on schema/ gen OWL, SHACL, JSON-LD context and Markdown docs into build/ and docs/schema/ rdf converts the YAML examples to Turtle in build/rdf/ mappings validates SSSOM files and converts them to RDF spex exports queries as SIB SPARQL examples into build/sparql-examples/ test the pytest suite: every valid example validates, every invalid one is rejected, RDF conforms to the SHACL shapes, mappings are valid, and every competency question returns its expected result

make validate and make shacl run the first two checks on their own, which is handy when editing data. To browse the docs locally, run make docs-serve.

docs.title: 3. Run a competency question
docs.text:
python scripts/run_cq.py              # list all questions
python scripts/run_cq.py uc3-cq02     # run one

taxon          taxonLabel                    nStudies  directions           status
NCBITaxon:817  Bacteroides fragilis          2         decreased|increased  conflicting
NCBITaxon:562  Escherichia coli              1         increased            single study
...

Try an ad-hoc query: copy a .rq file, edit it, then run python scripts/run_cq.py --query my.rq.

docs.title: 4. Typical contributions
docs.text:
Add data for a use case

  1. Edit examples/valid/Container-ucN-*.yaml.
  2. Look up identifiers in OLS and paste the CURIE, e.g. ENVO:00002005.
  3. Quote dates: "2024-02-10".
  4. Run make validate.
  5. Run make slims when you use new ontology terms. It needs internet access and updates examples/ontology-slims/, which you commit. (make terms, which checks that each term sits in the right ontology branch, needs pip install -e ".[terms]" and downloads whole ontologies, so it is optional.)

Add a competency question

  1. Add a .rq file and an entry in queries/ucN-*/cqs.yaml.
  2. Add toy data that should produce an answer.
  3. Run python scripts/run_cq.py <id>. Check the output by hand, then write it with --write-expected.
  4. Run make test.

Change the schema

  1. Edit the relevant schema/*.yaml module.
  2. Run make lint validate test.
  3. If the change is a design decision, add a note in docs/adr/.

Add or review mappings. See VERDANT integration.

docs.title: Use cases and competency questions
docs.text:
Competency questions (CQs) are the questions the knowledge graph must be able to answer. Each has a SPARQL query, toy data designed to exercise it, and an expected result checked in CI.

Use case Queries Toy data UC1 Aeromicrobiome functional characterisation queries/uc1-aeromicrobiome/ examples/valid/Container-uc1-aeromicrobiome.yaml UC2 Antimicrobial resistance transmission queries/uc2-amr-transmission/ examples/valid/Container-uc2-amr.yaml UC3 Host–microbiome interactions in cancer queries/uc3-host-microbiome-cancer/ examples/valid/Container-uc3-cancer.yaml UC4 Metabolic impact of nutrition queries/uc4-nutrition-metabolism/ examples/valid/Container-uc4-nutrition.yaml

UC3 is the most complete one; copy its structure.

The team's own use cases and competency questions are in the project's coordination sheet and differ from the four below. How they map onto this schema, and what would need adding, is in Competency questions from the coordination sheet. In short: sheet use case 1 (clouds) corresponds to UC1, sheet use case 2 (plasmids in cancer) spans UC2 and UC3, UC4 has no counterpart in the sheet, and the sheet's macaque and crop-biocontrol use cases are new.

docs.title: Proposing a new competency question
docs.text:
A good question:

  • names the entities involved (taxon, habitat, disease…) and the context that matters (body site, time, place);
  • includes a concrete example answer from your domain, so toy data can be written;
  • says which existing resource could supply real data (e.g. MGnify, CARD, gutMDisorder).

Then add the query, toy data and expected result (see Onboarding).

docs.title: VERDANT integration (Project 11)
docs.text:
VERDANT builds AI-generated SKOS mappings (exactMatch, closeMatch, relatedMatch) from vocabulary terms to ontologies and knowledge bases, with an expert pre-check loop and a federated SPARQL endpoint.

This page sketches how data could flow between the two projects. Nothing here has been agreed with the VERDANT team.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[MiCoKnowGraph<br/>unmapped labels TSV] --> B[VERDANT<br/>embeddings + FAISS]
  B --> C[SKOS + confidence<br/>or SSSOM]
  C -->|scripts/skos_to_sssom.py| D[mappings/verdant/candidates/]
  D -->|PR review| E[mappings/curated/]
  D -->|PR review| F[mappings/verdant/rejected/<br/>predicate_modifier: Not]
  F -->|feedback / training data| B
  E -->|make mappings| G[(KG: skos:exactMatch triples)]

docs.title: 1. MiCoKnowGraph → VERDANT
docs.text:
Proposed format for the terms we would send (no script produces this yet):

column example term_id micokg:term/habitat/sewage label sewage context_slot env_medium source_kg infores:gutmdisorder suggested_target_ontology ENVO

Sources: - free-text habitat, sample-type, host and disease labels from existing microbiome KGs; - labels found when real data is loaded.

The three directories under mappings/ are curated/ (reviewed, loaded into the KG), verdant/candidates/ (unreviewed VERDANT output) and verdant/rejected/.

docs.title: 2. VERDANT → MiCoKnowGraph
docs.text:
Preferred: SSSOM TSV. Also accepted: Turtle with plain SKOS triples, or reified owl:Axiom mappings with sssom:confidence. See tests/fixtures/verdant-sample.ttl.

python scripts/skos_to_sssom.py verdant-output.ttl \
  -o mappings/verdant/candidates/habitat.sssom.tsv \
  --mapping-set-id https://w3id.org/micokg/mappings/verdant/habitat \
  --tool-version 0.3.0

Every candidate row gets: - mapping_justification: semapv:SemanticSimilarityThresholdMatching - mapping_tool: VERDANT - the tool version and a confidence score - no reviewer_id

docs.title: 3. Review
docs.text:
Reviewers go through candidates in a pull request:

Decision Action Accept Move the row to mappings/curated/<topic>.sssom.tsv, put your ORCID in reviewer_id, keep the original confidence Accept with a different predicate As accept, change predicate_id (e.g. exact → close), and explain in comment Reject Move the row to mappings/verdant/rejected/, add a predicate_modifier column set to Not, and give the reason in comment

Rejected rows are published so VERDANT can use them as negative training examples.

docs.title: 4. How mappings are used in the KG
docs.text:
• make mappings validates SSSOM files and writes plain skos:exactMatch / closeMatch triples. The CLI's own output is reified owl:Axioms, which are hard to query.
  • Queries expand identifiers with ?disease (skos:exactMatch|^skos:exactMatch)?/rdfs:subClassOf* ?queryDisease. See queries/uc3-host-microbiome-cancer/cq01-*.rq.
  • Only curated mappings are loaded into the KG used by tests. Candidates are not.

docs.title: Open points to agree with VERDANT
docs.text:
1. The identifier scheme for free-text labels, i.e. who mints micokg:term/... IDs.
  2. Target ontologies and versions: ENVO, UBERON, NCBITaxon, MONDO, ChEBI, FoodOn?
  3. Confidence calibration: is 0.8 comparable across target ontologies?
  4. Endpoint URL, and whether MiCoKnowGraph example queries should be loaded there (SIB sh:SPARQLExecutable files from make spex).
  5. Update cadence and versioning of mapping sets.

docs.title: ADR-0001: Represent associations as nodes (reification), with derived shortcut edges
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Microbiome findings depend on context. The same taxon can be reported as increased in colorectal-cancer stool and decreased in tumour tissue. It can also be associated in one cohort and not in another, or depend on the sequencing method. Downstream users (curators, meta-analysts, graph-ML pipelines) need to know direction, body site, environment, host, evidence type and source for every claim. They also need to see disagreement instead of having it hidden.

A direct edge such as NCBITaxon:817 RO:0002610 MONDO:0005575 can hold none of this. Two contradictory findings collapse into one triple.

Options considered:

  1. Direct edges only. Simple queries and a small graph, but context and provenance are lost.
  2. Named graph per source. Provenance only at dataset level; still no per-claim direction or body site.
  3. RDF-star / RDF 1.2 triple terms. Elegant, but support across triple stores (and federation with VERDANT's endpoint) is still uneven.
  4. Association nodes (the n-ary relation pattern used by Biolink, the Semanticscience Integrated Ontology (SIO) and KG-Microbe). Each claim is a resource with rdf:subject, rdf:predicate, rdf:object and context slots.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Use option 4 as the source of truth, and add a derived layer of direct edges:

  • Every claim is an instance of a subclass of Association (schema/associations.yaml).
  • scripts/materialise_shortcuts.rq builds ?s ?p ?o edges into the named graph <https://w3id.org/micokg/graph/shortcuts>. It leaves out negated associations and those with confidence below 0.5.
  • Raw per-sample measurements are SOSA Observations. Associations can point back to them with prov:wasDerivedFrom.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Pro: Conflicting and context-dependent findings coexist and can be queried (uc3-cq02).
  • Pro: It aligns with Biolink / KG-Microbe / MicrobiomeKG, so crosswalks are cheap.
  • Pro: Graph-ML users can take the shortcut graph, and use association attributes as edge features.
  • Con: Queries are longer: 3 triple patterns per hop instead of 1.
  • Con: More triples. This is acceptable at the expected scale; revisit if needed.
  • Con: Shortcut thresholds (confidence ≥ 0.5, not negated) are a policy that needs community agreement.

docs.title: ADR-0002: Identifiers, IRIs and ontology-valued slots
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Integration only works if the same thing has the same identifier everywhere. The blueprint also has to produce RDF that SPARQL can traverse, including ontology hierarchies. Early prototyping showed two technical pitfalls:

  • LinkML serialises enum values as string literals in RDF, so they can't be linked to ontology hierarchies.
  • Class-typed ranges make the generated SHACL require every referenced ontology term to be typed in the data, which contributors would find tedious.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Reuse ontology identifiers for biological, chemical, environmental and disease entities. Mint micokg:<type>/<local-id> only for instance data (samples, observations, associations, studies, hosts, gene records).
  2. Namespace: https://w3id.org/micokg/. The w3id redirect is to be registered once the GitHub organisation is agreed.
  3. Ontology-valued slots use range: uriorcurie plus a prefix pattern, and optionally bindings to a dynamic enum for branch checks. They are serialised as IRIs, and a test enforces this.
  4. Expand prefixes to OBO PURLs (http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/ENVO_), matching the ontologies' own IRIs. The canonical_prefixes lint rule (identifiers.org) is disabled.
  5. Preferred prefixes per entity:
Entity Prefixes Taxon NCBITaxon; GTDB accepted for MAG-derived taxa Disease MONDO preferred; DOID, NCIT and EFO accepted and bridged by SSSOM (to be decided: the proposal names DO) Metabolite CHEBI (HMDB accepted) Habitat / environment ENVO Anatomy UBERON Function GO; KEGG orthology and EC as gene families AMR ARO Food FOODON (CHEBI for defined compounds) Evidence ECO

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Pro: Data from different resources joins on identifiers, not labels.
  • Pro: Queries can use rdfs:subClassOf* over ontology slims or full ontologies.
  • Con: YAML patterns check the prefix only, not whether the term exists or sits in the right branch. make terms runs linkml-term-validator for that.
  • Con: SHACL sh:pattern constraints written for CURIEs don't apply to expanded IRIs, so they are dropped when validating RDF (see tests/test_rdf_shacl.py).

docs.title: ADR-0003: Ontology reuse and the use of slims
docs.text:
• Status: Proposed
  • Date: 2026-09-15

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The proposal names GO, ENVO, DO, SOSA, SIO, NCIT, UBERON, EFO and DCT, and the use cases add NCBITaxon, ChEBI, ARO, SO, FoodOn, ECO, OBI and MIxS.

  • Importing whole ontologies into the schema is heavy (NCBITaxon alone is several GB) and makes CI slow.
  • Queries still need hierarchy information, e.g. "colorectal adenocarcinoma is a colorectal cancer".
  • Java/ROBOT tooling is not available to all contributors.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
1. Reference ontologies by identifier; don't import them into the LinkML schema.
  2. Standard vocabularies for properties:
Vocabulary Used for MIxS Sample environment slots SOSA Observations RO Biological relations DCTERMS / PROV Provenance SKOS Mappings SIO is about; association class mapping
  1. Slims for tests. scripts/build_slims.py collects the is_a ancestors and labels of every term used in examples and curated mappings from the EBI OLS API, into examples/ontology-slims/*.ttl. The slims are committed, so tests run offline in seconds.
  2. Production deployments should load full ontologies, or federate with a service that holds them (e.g. Ubergraph), instead of relying on slims.
  3. Branch checks. Dynamic enums in schema/enums.yaml (reachable_from) describe the allowed branch for each slot. They are checked by make terms (needs network access), not in CI.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Pro: Pure-Python tooling with fast, offline CI.
  • Pro: Which ontologies are preferred can change without schema churn.
  • Con: Slims have to be rebuilt (make slims) when new terms are used. make terms checks for drift.
  • Con: Ontology structure can surprise. For example, in SO, plasmid is not a subclass of mobile_genetic_element, so query authors must check hierarchies in OLS.

docs.text:
